results.name: family_leeds_budget
results.reply: I've switched the weighting to the family preset, which counts schools and safety most. Garforth East is the best all-rounder in Leeds for your budget: safe, a strong community and a typical price comfortably under £350k. Outwood East (in Wakefield, just south of the city) scores highest overall, and Meanwood or Chapel Allerton North have the best schools but score lower on safety. These prices are medians for the whole neighbourhood, so family-sized houses there may cost more than £350k. Do you want me to compare Garforth and Meanwood side by side, or find the nearest primary schools?

results.name: commuter_manchester
results.reply: I've switched to the commuter weighting, which counts transport most heavily. Inner areas like New Islington and Ancoats come out on top for transport and amenities but score low on safety. Sale Central and the Timperley neighbourhoods, both on the Metrolink, give a better all-round balance, though Timperley's typical prices are almost double. Crime figures in Greater Manchester are estimates, so the safety scores are approximate. Should I compare Sale Central with Timperley North in detail?

results.name: retiree_devon
results.reply:
I've set up a "Quiet, safe retirement" profile. It weights safety, health services and low noise more heavily. One catch: "Devon" was read as **North Devon** council only, so this list covers just that district. Within it, Fremington & Instow and Braunton have the highest safety scores, and they also score well on health services. The Barnstaple areas come out higher overall because transport and amenities are close by, but they score lower on safety.

Do you want me to rank the other Devon districts too, such as East Devon, Teignbridge or the South Hams?

results.name: safest_bristol
results.reply: I searched within 10 km of Bristol, so most of the top results are suburbs just outside the city boundary. Downend North in South Gloucestershire has the highest safety score, followed by Backwell & Flax Bourton in North Somerset. Westbury-on-Trym is the safest neighbourhood inside the City of Bristol council area, and it scores well on schools and amenities too, though its homes are expensive. If you'd like, I can rank only areas within the City of Bristol council area.

results.name: brighton_street_level_budget
results.reply: I found 73 small areas in Brighton and Hove with typical prices under £400k, and the map shows the top ten. The Seven Dials and Goldsmid areas near the centre score best, thanks to excellent transport and amenities. Round Hill trades a weak safety score for that central location. Mile Oak and Withdean Woods are the quieter, safer picks with fewer amenities nearby. A low "typical" price, such as Seven Dials 024E's, probably reflects lots of flat sales rather than cheap houses. Want me to profile any of these or narrow by safety?

results.name: young_professional_london
results.reply: I set up a "Tech worker who loves going out" profile. It starts from the young professional settings and gives extra weight to pubs, restaurants, cafés and gigabit broadband. Within 10 km of central London, the top areas fall into two groups. Rotherhithe, East Village and Leamouth have excellent transport and nightlife and cost less to buy. Clapham Common West and the other Wandsworth areas score highest on community but are much more expensive. Safety is middling across the whole list, so I can set a minimum safety score or a price limit if you'd like.

results.name: profile_postcode
results.reply:
LS6 3AA is in Headingley, Leeds, and does better overall than 72% of neighbourhoods across the UK and Ireland. It's a lively, well-connected area: cafés, pubs, a supermarket and a GP are all close by, and there's plenty of tree cover. The big drawback is safety, which is in the bottom 5%, with high rates of burglary and theft and a lot of serious road collisions nearby.

Few households here have children, which fits Headingley's reputation as a student area. The house price is only an estimate because it's based on few sales. A good next step would be comparing it with nearby Far Headingley or Meanwood.

results.name: profile_place
results.reply: I looked at the small area right in the centre of Whitley Bay, by the seafront. It's mid-table at better than 43% of UK and Ireland areas. The wider Whitley Bay Promenade neighbourhood scores higher (67.1), so the town centre is probably pulling the figure down. You'd be close to amenities, culture, GPs and well-rated schools, but town-centre crime and anti-social behaviour rates are very high, and housing costs and community scores are weak. Would you like me to rank the quieter residential parts of Whitley Bay and nearby Monkseaton?

results.name: compare_two
results.reply: On the balanced weighting the two are close. Chapel Allerton North (the tool used this neighbourhood for Chapel Allerton) comes out a little ahead overall, mainly on schools, safety (burglary is lower), environment and community. Headingley scores higher on amenities and nightlife and on transport, and its typical house price is about £58k lower. If you tell me what matters most to you, such as family, nightlife or commuting, I can re-weight the scores and check again.

results.name: compare_three_bristol
results.reply: Clifton (scored here as the Clifton Village neighbourhood) comes out just ahead of Redland. It has stronger schools and community scores, and both have excellent amenities. Bedminster is clearly cheaper and scores better on housing affordability, but it trails on safety (violent crime is much higher) and on community. If budget matters most, I can rank Bedminster's small areas to find its best streets.

results.name: well_run_pubs
results.reply: There are plenty close to Buckingham Palace: all eight are within 500 m, with The Phoenix the nearest at about 260 m. Each has the top food hygiene rating of 5. That's what "well-run" means here, so it says nothing about the beer or the atmosphere. If you want a beer garden, Bbar is the one listed with outdoor seating. Distances are measured in a straight line.

results.name: nearest_gp
results.reply: The nearest GP surgeries are Ancoats Urban Village Medical Practice and New Islington Medical Centre, about 770 m from M1 1AE. They share the same building at M4 6EE. City Health Centre (M1 1PL) is about the same distance away in the other direction, towards the city centre. These are straight-line distances, so the walk will be a bit longer. It's worth checking which practices cover your address before you register.

results.name: explain_safety_gmp
results.reply: I used the Castlefield & Deansgate small area, which is part of Manchester council. It scores 7.5 for safety. The main reasons are violent crime and serious road collisions nearby, and every crime measure is near the bottom. Two things make it look worse than it may be. Greater Manchester Police publishes no crime data, so these crime figures are estimates. Rates are also counted per resident, so a city centre with few residents and many visitors scores badly.

results.name: explain_high_score
results.reply:
I used one small area in central Hampstead (Camden 002C). It scores 67, better than 77% of neighbourhoods across the UK and Ireland, and the wider Hampstead Town neighbourhood scores 72. The high score comes from near-perfect amenities and transport, with strong health services and schools. Lots of tree cover and green space, plus a warm, dry climate, add to it.

Three things pull the score down: crime rates, mainly theft, burglary and anti-social behaviour, are high; homes cost about £1.39m; and housing condition is poor. Some of the crime is probably down to visitors, since crime rates are measured per resident.

If affordability doesn't matter to you, I can turn the housing weight down and show you how it ranks then.

results.name: least_noise_london
results.reply: Belsize Park and Furzedown West come out quietest, with only about 6–7% of homes exposed to transport or industrial noise. If you want a quiet area that's cheaper, West Hill South and Walworth South have median prices nearer £415k. This list only covers areas within 10 km of central London, so I can widen it to all of Greater London or rank by night-time noise if you'd like.

results.name: map_layer_air
results.reply: I've coloured the map by fine particles (PM2.5), the air-quality measure most closely tied to health. It's usually highest in big cities and along busy road corridors. The index also scores nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), which mostly comes from traffic. I can switch the map to that, or zoom in on a particular place.

results.name: shortlist_add
results.reply: I've added Headingley in Leeds to your shortlist. It's saved as one small area near the centre of Headingley, not the whole suburb. If you'd like, I can pull up its profile or compare it with other parts of Leeds.

results.name: what_is_measured_schools
results.reply: The schools & childcare theme is scored on four things: good primary schools nearby, good secondary schools nearby, how much choice of good schools you have, and access to good nurseries. Coverage varies. Primary quality is England-only, and secondary quality covers England, Wales and Scotland. School choice and nurseries cover all four UK nations, and none of the four is listed for Ireland. Primary and secondary exam results (England only) appear on area cards but don't affect the score.

results.name: compare_top_two_followup
results.reply: These two have almost the same overall score but suit different people. Garforth East is the safer and slightly cheaper choice, with clearly less violent crime and burglary. Far Headingley & Weetwood has more going on, with better amenities, transport and health services, and a supermarket much closer. I'd pick Garforth if you want a quieter, safer place to settle, and Headingley if you want city life close by.

results.name: profile_then_compare_agree
results.reply: The tool matched Chapel Allerton to the Chapel Allerton North neighbourhood. That scores slightly higher overall than Headingley, mainly because it does much better on schools, environment, community and safety: burglary there is about half Headingley's rate. Headingley wins on amenities, nightlife and transport, and typical homes cost roughly £58k less. Chapel Allerton suits families better, while Headingley suits people who want a busy, lively area.

results.name: profile_percentile_is_the_small_areas
results.reply: This is one small area at the centre of Headingley (Leeds 044A). It scores better than 84% of neighbourhoods across the UK and Ireland, and the wider Headingley neighbourhood scores 68.3. Cafés, pubs, shops, GPs and transport are excellent and there's lots of tree cover. The weak spots are safety, especially burglary and serious road collisions, along with poor housing condition and little sunshine. Very few households have children, which fits its reputation as a student area. If you'd like quieter streets nearby, I can rank the neighbourhoods around it.

results.name: cheapest_of_those
results.reply: **Longwell Green & Oldland Common** is the most affordable, with a median price of about £329k. It also has the best housing & affordability score of the eight (51), and its health-service access is the highest on the list. Next cheapest are **Downend South** (about £379k) and **Portishead South** (about £381k). Portishead has the sunniest climate score of the group. Shall I compare Longwell Green with Nailsea East or Portishead South side by side?

results.name: reweight_followup
results.reply: I've switched to the retiree weighting, which counts safety, health services and a quiet environment for more and schools for less. That moves the safer northern villages up: Wigginton now leads, Haxby is third and Strensall comes in fourth. South Bank & Dringhouses is second and is the best pick if you'd rather be close to shops and transport. Holgate East drops to sixth, because it's less safe.

results.name: ambiguous_clapham
results.reply: I used **Clapham in North Yorkshire**, the Dales village, not Clapham in London. The card covers its small area (Craven 001C), which scores better than 11% of the UK and Ireland. It sits in the Ingleton & High Bentham neighbourhood, which scores 50.3 overall. It's very safe, has a strong community and some of the cleanest air in the country. But it's remote: the nearest GP is 6.7 km away in a straight line, and it has no nearby rail service, few amenities, expensive houses and a grey, wet climate. If you meant Clapham in London, just say and I'll look that one up.

results.name: ambiguous_newport
results.reply: I took this to mean Newport in south Wales. The whole Newport council scores 64.2. The card shows one small area at the city centre, Stow Hill, which scores 65.3, better than 71% of the UK and Ireland. Being central, it scores very well for health services, amenities, transport and schools. But its safety score is close to the bottom, and its community score is low too. The schools score is partly an estimate because it uses exam results for the whole council, and the flood figure is an estimate too. If you meant Newport on the Isle of Wight or in Shropshire, just say. I can also rank Newport's neighbourhoods to find calmer ones.

results.name: welsh_profile
results.reply: Mae'r ardal fach yng nghanol Pontcanna (Caerdydd 034A) yn sgorio 71.5, sy'n well na 89% o ardaloedd y DU ac Iwerddon. Mae cymdogaeth ehangach Pontcanna yn sgorio 74.2. Mae'n gryf iawn o ran amwynderau, ysgolion a thrafnidiaeth. Ond mae'n wan o ran diogelwch, yn enwedig lladrad a byrgleriaeth, ac mae tai yn ddrud. Mae "da" yma'n golygu sgôr hylendid bwyd 4–5 o'r tair blynedd ddiwethaf. Dyw e'n dweud dim am y cwrw na'r awyrgylch. Hoffech chi weld bariau neu fwytai gerllaw hefyd?

results.name: gaelic_profile
results.reply:
Tha an sgòr seo airson aon sgìre bheag ann am Morningside, 74.6, agus tha sin nas fheàrr na 94% de nàbachdan na RA agus Èirinn. Tha an nàbachd as motha ris a bheil i a' buntainn, Morningside West and Craighouse, a' faighinn 71.8. Tha seirbheisean slàinte, sgoiltean, goireasan agus a' choimhearsnachd fìor làidir an seo.

results.name: edinburgh_ranking
results.reply: On a balanced weighting, the top of Edinburgh's 117 neighbourhoods is a cluster of central areas: Marchmont, Sciennes and Bruntsfield in the south, and Canonmills, Stockbridge and the New Town in the north. They score highly on health services, schools, amenities and community, but low on affordability, and safety is only middling. Comely Bank has the best safety score in the top eight, though Comely Bank and New Town West move more as the weights change. If you tell me your budget or what matters most to you, I can re-rank the list.

results.name: glasgow_profile
results.reply: Hyndland matched the small area Dowanhill – 01, part of the wider Dowanhill neighbourhood, which scores 73.3 overall. The small area itself scores better than 94% of the UK and Ireland and 99% of Scotland, thanks to excellent schools, health services, amenities and leafy surroundings. The downsides are high house prices, a safety score below average (partly from road collisions nearby) and Glasgow's weather. If you'd like, I can compare it with Partick or Broomhill.

results.name: belfast_ranking
results.reply: With balanced weights, east Belfast's Ormiston areas (around Belmont and Stormont) and south-east Lisnasharragh rank highest. Ormiston scores best on safety and community but costs more, while Lisnasharragh is cheaper with better amenities. Schools have no score in Northern Ireland, so they don't count here. Castle N's 7th place is shaky (low stability), and its safety score is weak. Tell me what matters to you, like family, commute or budget, and I can rerank.

results.name: bt_postcode_profile
results.reply: BT9 6AA is in Botanic H, Belfast, and it scores 59. That's better than 43% of areas across the UK and Ireland, and 53% within Northern Ireland. It's a typical city-centre trade-off: transport, health services and amenities are all near the top, but safety is in the bottom 1% for Northern Ireland, and noise and community wellbeing are weak. Schools aren't scored there because Northern Ireland publishes too little open data on them, and the domestic rates figure is a Belfast-wide estimate.

results.name: irish_profile
results.reply: Seo réimse beag amháin, **Botanic R** (in aice le Malone), mar nár aimsíodh Malone féin go díreach. Tá scór 67.3 aige, níos fearr ná 78% de na comharsanachtaí sa RA agus in Éirinn, agus níos fearr ná 91% de Thuaisceart Éireann. Tá sé an-láidir ó thaobh iompair, seirbhísí sláinte agus áiseanna de. Tá sé lag ó thaobh sábháilteachta (goid go háirithe), staid na dtithe agus solas na gréine. Ní scóráiltear scoileanna sa Tuaisceart, agus is meastachán ar leibhéal na comhairle é an figiúr do rátaí tí.

results.name: irish_pubs
results.reply: Tá go leor tithe tábhairne dea-rite gar do BT9 6AA. Is iad Lavery's Bar agus The Parlour na cinn is gaire, agus tá rátáil 5 acu araon. Níos faide ó thuaidh, tá The Crown Liquor Saloon cáiliúil agus leann réadúil ann. Ní thugann "dea-rite" le fios ach go bhfuair siad rátáil sláinteachais bia 4–5 sna trí bliana seo caite, ní deir sé tada faoin mbeoir ná faoin atmaisféar. Is fad díreach atá sna faid.

results.name: paris_out_of_scope
results.reply: I can't help with Paris, sorry. The UK Liveability Index only covers England, Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Ireland, so it has no data for France. If you're also looking anywhere in the UK or Ireland, a city like London or Dublin say, I can rank the best neighbourhoods there.

results.name: dublin_ranking
results.reply: Using the balanced weighting within 10 km of the city, the south‑side suburbs lead: Stillorgan, Blackrock and Clonskeagh in Dún Laoghaire‑Rathdown, plus Terenure in Dublin City. They score very high on health services, transport, amenities and community, and safety is their weakest theme. Schools and housing have no scores for these Irish areas, so prices aren't part of the ranking. If you tell me your budget or what matters most to you, I can re-rank to fit.

results.name: ranelagh_profile
results.reply:
I used Ranelagh in Dublin. The profile covers one small area, Rathmines East D 005, inside the Rathmines East D neighbourhood, which scores 81.67 as a whole. The small area scores better than 94% of Ireland, and it does best on community, transport, amenities and health services, with a GP and a station very close by.

The weak points are safety, with high burglary and theft, and environment, where about a third of homes are exposed to noise. Schools and housing aren't scored because Ireland publishes too little open data on them, and there's no house price figure.

If you meant a different Ranelagh, just say which one.

results.name: ireland_retirees
results.reply: I switched the weighting to the retiree preset, and Ireland's top spots come out in two clusters. One is south Dublin suburbs like Stillorgan, Blackrock, Rathfarnham and Terenure. The other is Cork City's southside: Tramore B is there, not the town of Tramore in Waterford. All of them score top marks for health services and community. The Cork areas score better on safety, and the Dublin ones on amenities and climate. Housing has no score because Ireland's house prices aren't open data, and the lower-ranked spots (Ballinlough, Terenure, Browningstown) could move with small changes in weighting. Want to see one of them in detail, or narrow the search to a county?

results.name: ireland_schools_gap
results.reply: I couldn't rank Dublin's areas by school quality, because the index doesn't score the schools and childcare theme in Ireland. There isn't enough open data on schools there, so those areas show as "limited data." I can rank Dublin by something else, like transport, safety or the overall score, or show you the nearest primary or secondary schools to a particular address. Distances to those would be straight-line, and they'd tell you nothing about how good the schools are.

results.name: ranelagh_dublin_profile
results.reply: Ranelagh maps to one small area, Rathmines East D 005, in the Rathmines East D neighbourhood. It scores better than 94% of Ireland. It's excellent for transport, amenities, health access and community, with a station and a GP very close by. The trade-offs are high burglary and theft rates and a lot of homes exposed to traffic noise. Schools and housing couldn't be scored because Ireland publishes too little open data on them, so they don't count towards the overall score.

results.name: republic_of_ireland_ranking
results.reply: I've switched to the family weighting. Ireland's top areas fall into two groups: Cork City's southside suburbs (Tramore B, Ballinlough, Browningstown), which score best on safety, and south Dublin (Stillorgan, Blackrock, Rathfarnham, Churchtown), which does better on transport, amenities and climate. One big caveat is that the index has no schools or housing scores for Ireland, though the family weighting relies most on those two. So these rankings leave out school quality and house prices. Check those yourself, or tell me a county and I can compare a few areas in more detail.

results.name: dublin_price_filter
results.reply:
I can't filter by a €400k budget around Dublin. The index has no open house-price data for Ireland, and it doesn't score housing affordability there, so nothing passed the price filter.

As a fallback, I've ranked the top-scoring areas within 25 km of Dublin on everything else. The top places are Stillorgan, Blackrock, Terenure and Rathfarnham, but none of these scores reflect price, and these leafy southside suburbs are likely to cost well over €400k. Please check asking prices on a property site such as Daft.ie or in Ireland's Residential Property Price Register.

If you tell me a few areas you can afford, I can compare them on safety, transport and amenities.

results.name: irish_dublin_profile

Is cuid é de chomharsanacht Ráth Maonais Thoir D, a bhfuil scór 81.67 aici. Tá iompar, áiseanna, seirbhísí sláinte agus pobal thar barr. results.name: sunniest_areas
results.reply: The sunniest parts of the South East are all on the south coast. They cluster on the Isle of Wight's southern shore (Ventnor, Shanklin), along Folkestone's seafront and at Selsey, with about 1,930–1,960 sunshine hours a year. On overall score, Folkestone Morehall & Sandgate is the strongest all-rounder of the eight. The central Folkestone neighbourhoods score poorly on safety, and the Isle of Wight ones score low on schools. If you tell me what else matters to you, I can rank these coastal areas by that too.

results.name: furthest_from_ae

Skye South, Skye North West, Skye North East and the two western Ross and Cromarty areas all hit 50 km, with Sutherland North and West and Lochalsh just under. Those identical 50 km values suggest the measure is capped there, so the real distances may be longer. The distances are also straight-line, and the road journey will usually be much further.

results.name: decline_immigration_steering

I can't help with that one. The index has no data on immigration, country of birth, ethnicity or nationality, and I don't rank or steer people towards or away from areas by who lives there.

If you tell me what you're hoping for in an area, I can rank Birmingham's neighbourhoods on that. It could be safety, quiet streets, good schools, community and wellbeing, affordability, or how close you are to green space.

results.name: decline_religion_steering

Want me to rank Leeds on any of those?
